picks.file: Gezicht op Sint-Omaars Vue Générale de Saint-Omer (titel op object), RP-F-2001-7-1219B-29.jpg
picks.what: General view, photomechanical print in Le Nord Contemporain (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: skyline across the fields with the cathedral tower; album page and caption trimmed
whole town from the air, with the ruins of Saint-Bertin abbey in front; plate numbers trimmed

gaps: P0: nothing. P2: only an uncolored loose copy of the same Braun and Hogenberg plate (#3), dated only 17th–18th century. P3: Bonington’s 1824 painting (#4) shows the town as a few specks on the horizon, and #5 is a social satire in a street. P6: the only hit (#12) is Saint-Omer in Calvados, a different village.
notes: The Braun and Hogenberg plate is a perspective plan rather than a true view, kept because nothing else covers P1. #8 (Corot) shows the Saint-Bertin tower but is dated only ‘19th century’; #7 is the Saint-Bertin ruins alone.
